title: Beijing Sees One Theater. Washington Should, Too
gist: A CNAS commentary (excerpt, originally in WPS Dispatch) argues US deterrence in the Pacific is fraying as Trump sends mixed signals and the Iran war drains critical munitions, while Beijing intensifies gray-zone coercion against Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines as one connected campaign across a single theater; restoring deterrence requires clearer commitments to resist China's coercion and the credible means to back them.

insights.claim: US deterrence in the Pacific is fraying, and restoring it requires clearer commitments to resist China's coercion plus the means to make those commitments credible.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: A stated deterrence gap that needs 'the means to make them credible' argues for sustained Indo-Pacific defense investment and munitions replenishment.
insights.quote: U.S. deterrence in the Pacific is fraying. Restoring it requires clearer commitments to resist China’s coercion, and the means to make them credible.
insights.locator: This article was originally published in WPS Dispatch.

insights.claim: As Trump sends mixed signals and the Iran war drains critical US munitions, Beijing is intensifying pressure on Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines to test whether Washington will act or settle for statements.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Iran-war munition depletion directly weakens Pacific deterrence—an explicit link between the Middle East campaign and China-risk in Asia.
insights.quote: As President Trump sends mixed signals and the Iran war drains critical U.S. munitions, Beijing is intensifying pressure on Taiwan, Japan, and the Philippines
insights.locator: As President Trump sends mixed signals

insights.claim: CNAS frames China's gray-zone warfare against Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines—plus its efforts to control the seas and straits between them—as a single coercive campaign across one connected theater, where each unanswered provocation erodes confidence in Washington's resolve across the First Island Chain.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Treating the First Island Chain as one theater implies contagion of credibility—a loss anywhere reprices US resolve everywhere, raising cross-regional escalation risk.
insights.quote: reflect a single coercive campaign across one connected theater
insights.locator: China’s gray-zone warfare against all three

insights.claim: CNAS argues giving Taiwan the means to remain free is not a call for war but how the US deters one, preserving peace along the First Island Chain and across the broader Indo-Pacific.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Framing Taiwan arms as deterrence, not provocation, supports continued US security assistance—a tailwind for Taiwan-defense procurement.
insights.quote: Giving Taiwan the means to remain free is not a call for war. It is how the United States deters one
insights.locator: Giving Taiwan the means to remain free
